11-180.r: Wrong pair: Harisena → Samudragupta (Prayag Prashasti), not Harsha, whose poet was Banabhatta. Correct: Ravi Kirti → Pulakesin II; Bhavabhuti → Yasovarman; Dandi → Narasimha Varman.

11-181.r: Court poets: Amir Khusro → Alauddin Khalji; Kalidas → Chandragupta II; Harisena → Samudragupta; Banabhatta → Harshvardhan.

11-182.r: Bhoj → Dhar; Durgawati → Gondwana; Samudragupta → Vidisha; Ashoka → Ujjain.

11-183.r: Correct: Bhilsa → Madhya Pradesh (Vidisha); Girinagar → Gujarat. Wrong: Dwarasamudra → Karnataka (Hoysala capital); Sthanesvara (Thanesar) → Haryana.

12-001.r: Khajuraho temples → Chandela dynasty; Chhatarpur district, MP; built 950-1050 AD; Kandariya Mahadev is the largest.

12-005.r: Khajuraho → group of Hindu and Jain temples built by the Chandelas (950-1050 AD); originally 85 temples.
12-005.t: Not only Hindu: Khajuraho has Jain temples too.

12-007.r: Matangeshvara Temple, Khajuraho → dedicated to Shiva; built in King Dhanga's reign; Nagara style.

12-008.r: Dashavatara Temple → at Deogarh (Lalitpur), Gupta period, not Khajuraho. Kandariya Mahadev, Chausath Yogini, Chitragupta temples → Khajuraho (Chandelas).

12-009.r: Chausath Yogini temple (Morena, MP) → circular, built by Kachchhapaghata king Devapala (1323 CE); thought to inspire India's Parliament design; not the only circular temple, not Vaishnava.

12-010.r: Stupa → Sanchi; Painting → Bagh; Headless statue of Kanishka → Mathura; Dashavatara Temple → Deogarh.

12-011.r: Not a World Heritage Site → Mandu fort. Khajuraho temples, Bhimbetka rock shelters and Sanchi stupa are UNESCO World Heritage Sites.

12-012.r: True: free-standing temples began in the Gupta period; early Ladkhan temple → Chalukyas of Badami; Khajuraho compartments linked inside and out. False: Kailashnath, Kanchi as earliest Dravida free-standing temple.

12-013.r: Teli Temple, Gwalior → Dravida-style shikhar (pinnacle) with Nagara-style ornamentation; a fusion of both styles.

12-014.r: Vesara (hybrid) style → Hoysaleshwara Temple, Halebidu (Karnataka): dark schist, star-like ground plans, rich carving; neither fully Dravida nor Nagara.

12-015.r: Kanheri caves (north of Borivali, Mumbai) → more than 100 Buddhist caves, from the 1st century BC.

12-016.r: Jain temple of Abu → made of marble; built by Vimal Shah, feudatory of Chalukya king Bheemdev I of Gujarat.

12-017.r: Palitana Jain temples → Shatrunjaya hill, Bhavnagar district, Gujarat; dedicated to the 1st Tirthankara, Adinatha.

12-018.r: Elephanta caves → mainly Shaiva (Lord Shiva); ascribed to the Rashtrakutas; five Hindu and two Buddhist caves; Trimurti of Shiva.

12-021.r: Ellora and Elephanta → Rashtrakuta period; Elephanta is famous for the Trimurti Shiva; Ellora has Hindu, Jain and Buddhist caves.

12-023.r: Gupta cave paintings survive at Ajanta and Bagh caves only; Lomas Rishi cave → Mauryan (Barabar hills); Nasik caves → Satavahana period.

12-024.r: Rock-cut caves of western India → Nasik (Pandavleni, Buddhist), Ellora (34 caves: Buddhist, Hindu, Jain) and Ajanta.

12-025.r: Buddhist cave temples → Ajanta; Elephanta → Shaiva; Khajuraho → Shaiva, Vaishnava and Jain temples; Nalanda → Buddhist education centre.

12-026.r: Ellora caves → mostly built by the Rashtrakuta rulers.

12-027.r: Only statement 3 true: Ellora has caves of different faiths (12 Buddhist, 17 Hindu, 5 Jain). Oldest are Bhimbetka shelters, not Badami; Ashoka, not Chandragupta, gave Barabar caves to Ajivikas.

12-028.r: Ellora (Verul Leni, near Chhatrapati Sambhaji Nagar) → caves of all three faiths: 1-12 Buddhist, 13-29 Hindu, 30-34 Jain.
12-028.h: Ellora order B-H-J: Buddhist first, Hindu middle, Jain last.

12-031.r: Rock-cut temple → Kailasa Temple, Ellora, built by Rashtrakuta ruler Krishna I in Dravidian style.

12-033.r: Wonder of rock-cut architecture → Kailasa Temple (Cave 16, Ellora), Dravidian style, built by Rashtrakuta king Krishna I; recalls Mount Kailasa, Shiva's home.
12-033.h: Cave 16, one rock, one king: Krishna I.

12-040.r: Rashtrakutas → patronised Shaiva, Vaishnava and Shakta faiths but leaned to Jainism; Amoghavarsha I was a disciple of Jain Acharya Jinasena (Adipuran).

12-041.r: Ajanta and Ellora caves → Chhatrapati Sambhaji Nagar (formerly Aurangabad) district, Maharashtra.

12-044.r: Gupta temples: brick temple → Bhitargaon; Dashavatara temple → Deogarh; Shiva temple → Bhumara; Vishnu temple → Eran.

12-045.r: Dashavatar temple, Deogarh (Lalitpur, near Jhansi; earliest Panchayatan temple of North India) and Garhwa sculptures (Shankargarh, Prayagraj) → Gupta art.

12-047.r: Bhitargaon temple (Kanpur) → Gupta-era terraced brick temple (5th-6th century AD) with terracotta panels; one of India's oldest brick temples; Nagara style. Both correct.

12-048.r: Ajanta art → mainly patronised by the Vakatakas (earlier caves from Satavahana period); Buddhist cave temples in Chhatrapati Sambhaji Nagar district.

12-049.r: Ajanta caves → Buddhist paintings of Jataka stories, mainly the Buddha's previous lives as a king.

12-050.r: Ajanta caves → gorge (valley) of the Waghora river. Sanchi lies west of the Betwa; Pandu-lena (Nashik) is in the Godavari valley.

12-051.r: Mural paintings → Ajanta caves and Lepakshi temple; not Sanchi Stupa (a hemispherical brick dome crowned by a Chhatra).

12-052.r: No Buddhist caves → Sanchi and Bulsar; Ajanta and Bagh have Buddhist caves. Both (c) and (d) accepted.

12-053.r: Pattachitra (Odisha) → Jagannath and Vaishnav themes; Manjusha (Bhagalpur, Bihar) → painted temple-shaped boxes of bamboo, jute, paper; Pithora → tribal ritual painting of Gujarat, MP.
12-053.c: Answer not printed; all three statements are true, but option (d) says 'all four', so no option fits.

12-054.r: Ajanta and Mahabalipuram share only rock-cut monuments; periods differ (Ajanta 2nd century BC-7th century AD; Mahabalipuram Pallava) and faiths differ (Buddhist vs Shiva/Vishnu).

12-055.r: Hampi → Karnataka; Nagarjunakonda → Andhra Pradesh; Shishupalgarh → Odisha; Arikamedu → Puducherry.

12-056.r: Konark Sun Temple (13th century, Odisha) → built by Narasimhadeva I (Eastern Ganga); solar chariot with twelve pairs of wheels, seven horses; 'Black Pagoda' (Puri Jagannath = 'White Pagoda').

12-060.r: Modhera Sun Temple (Patan, Gujarat) → built by Solanki king Bhimadeva I.

12-062.r: Lingaraja Temple → Bhubaneswar (Odisha); Shiva as 'Swayambhu' linga; about 180 ft high; finest Nagara-style example.

12-063.r: Lingaraja Temple → largest and tallest surviving temple in Odisha (about 180 ft).

12-064.r: Jagannath temple → Puri, Odisha; Odisha's temples (Lingaraj at Bhubaneswar, Konark) are in Nagara style.

12-066.r: Idols of Jagannath, Subhadra and Balbhadra at Puri → made of neem wood; repainted yearly and replaced about every 12 or 19 years.

12-067.r: Angkor Wat (Vishnu temple) → Cambodia (Kampuchea); built by Khmer king Suryavarman II in the early 12th century; world's largest religious structure.

12-070.r: Borobudur Stupa → Java island, Indonesia; a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
12-070.t: Angkor Wat is in Cambodia; Borobudur is in Java.

12-071.r: Gopuram (Dravida temples) → ornate, multi-storied tower over the gateway; began with the Pallavas, dominant by Pandya times.

12-072.r: Rock-cut temples and Rathas of Mahabalipuram → Pallavas (king Narasimha Varman); UNESCO site with Shore temple and Arjuna's penance.

12-074.r: Seven Ratha temples, Mahabalipuram → Pallava king Narasimhavarman I 'Mahamalla' (630-668 AD); city named after him; Mamalla style.

12-077.r: Smallest Ratha at Mahabalipuram → Draupadi Ratha (Mamalla style), with no ornamentation.

12-078.r: Kailasanathar Temple, Kanchipuram → built by Pallava king Narasimhavarman II in the Rajsimha style; dedicated to Shiva.

12-079.r: Temple order → Sapt Pagoda (Mamalla style), Shore Temple (Rajsimha style), Brihadeeswara (Rajaraja I), Gangaikonda Cholapuram (Rajendra I).
12-079.h: Two Pallava (Mamalla, then Rajsimha), then two Chola (Rajaraja, then Rajendra).

12-080.r: Elephanta → caves; Shravanabelagola → statue; Khajuraho → temples; Sanchi → stupa.

12-081.r: Bhimbetka → Madhya Pradesh; Shore temple → Tamil Nadu; Hampi → Karnataka; Manas → Assam.

12-082.r: Correct pair → Khajuraho Temple - Chandelas. Ellora's 34 caves are not Saka; Meenakshi Temple → Pandyas; Mahabalipuram → Pallavas.

12-083.r: Baidyanath Dham → Shiva temple; Sarnath → Buddha's first sermon; Dilwara → Jain temple; Badrinath → Vishnu temple (set up by Shankaracharya).
